text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: multiple ECC/PCIe AER errors and GPU resets on host gpu-node-12 (eu-west1). Severity: P1. Affected service: hosted-inference-prod (model/gpt-medium).

alice_oncall: Ack. I'm paged and on the thread. Starting triage. @bob_sre can you join?

alice_oncall: Quick customer summary — 5xx spike for /v1/generate ~18:13 UTC, impacting two enterprise tenants. Visible error rate ~7% for ~12m.

approx:incident-bot: Auto-run: collected first-level metrics and attached recent logs link: https://internal.artifacts/reports/1766209874 (perf/5xx/metrics).

bob_sre: On my way, ETA ~8m. What mitigations have you opened?

alice_oncall: I cordoned gpu-node-12 and started evicting pods: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12` then `kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — most inference pods are scheduling away, but a few stuck (local disks).

alice_oncall: Pasted kernel excerpt from node (dmesg):
```
[ 1392.421314] pcieport 0000:3a:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
[ 1392.421321] pcieport 0000:3a:00.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Data Link Layer, id=00e0(Transmitter ID)
[ 1392.421330] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1392.421391] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1393.012345] kernel: GPU reset succeeded, reinitializing
[ 1405.657488] pcieport 0000:3a:00.0: AER: Multiple corrected errors
```

carl_infra: Opening provider SR now. On provider console I'm seeing host hypervisor reboots around 18:17 UTC and a second short-lived reboot at 18:22 UTC. Suggesting host-level instability rather than a single GPU hardware fault. SR# 987654321 created with cloud vendor.

dana_ml: Customer impact: enterprise-42 and enterprise-77 reported degraded latency and occasional 5xx (retried). Estimate affected requests ~120k, failures ~8k. Not full outage but severe degradation for low-latency SLAs.

bob_sre: Taking over ops. Alice — thanks for cordon/drain. I'll continue collection and start a timeline + hypothesis list in-thread.

bob_sre: Commands I'm running now to collect host+gpu info:
```
gcloud compute ssh gpu-node-12 --zone=eu-west1 --command 'sudo journalctl -b -u kubelet -o short-iso > /tmp/node-kubelet.log'
sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-recent.log
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,PCI > /tmp/nvidia-q.log
sudo cp /var/log/messages /tmp/messages.log
```

bob_sre: Kernel excerpts (journalctl) show repeated PCIe AER corrected errors followed by GPU resets and then a host watchdog-triggered hv reboot. Example: `AER: Multiple Uncorrected error, logged` and `NVRM: Xid 31` around same time.

alice_oncall: Started tenant notifications: posting incident banner on status page and messaging enterprise-42/77 with initial blurb. Emily, can you help with customer comms updates once we have timeline?

emily_support: On it. Will draft update: short summary + mitigation steps + ETA for RCA.

bob_sre: Timeline (rough, UTC):
- 18:12:40 — metrics: increase in 5xx for /v1/generate (first alert)
- 18:13:05 — anomaly detector triggered, incident-bot paged oncall
- 18:14:10 — first corrected PCIe AER entries on gpu-node-12 dmesg
- 18:15:02 — first GPU reset (NVRM Xid 79) recorded
- 18:17:10 — hypervisor reboot recorded by cloud provider
- 18:18:30 — pods experiencing connection resets during migration; some failed to schedule due to local-data locks
- 18:22:05 — second short hypervisor restart observed (cloud provider)
- 18:25:00 — cordon/drain started; migration in progress
- 18:45:00 — provider confirms host flagged as unstable; live migration completed for most pods
- 19:05:00 — metrics recovering, 5xx returned to baseline

bob_sre: Hypotheses (in priority order):
1) Noisy neighbor or host-level PCIe fabric instability causing bursts of AERs -> GPU reset -> hypervisor-level watchdog -> host reboot. (Matches provider-reported host reboots.)
2) GPU card-level firmware regression leading to increased ECC/corrected errors culminating in resets.
3) Kernel/driver regression (recent node kernel or NVIDIA driver rollout) causing sensitivity to PCIe errors.
4) Cloud hypervisor bug (rare), e.g., degraded SR-IOV/VF passthrough interaction under load.

carl_infra: Provider SR update: vendor reproduced AER flood in hypervisor logs and flagged a noisy neighbor (other tenant) that was saturating PCIe root complex on that host. They are proposing live migrate affected VMs to new host and quarantine the host for deeper hardware diag. Requesting our logs for cross-correlation.

bob_sre: Actions assigned: 
- bob_sre -> collect and upload kernel/dmesg/nvidia-smi outputs to secure bucket (s3://redwood-incident-archives/1766209874/) — due 19:00 UTC
- carl_infra -> push logs to provider SR and request host reservation/quarantine — done, SR#987654321
- alice_oncall -> customer notifications + status page updates + link to postmortem draft — ongoing
- dana_ml -> run traffic replay tests against fallback model variant to confirm no model/regression errors — due 20:30 UTC
- emily_support -> prepare customer-facing timeline once we lock one — due 19:30 UTC

alice_oncall: FYI — I found that the nodes with repeated AERs are all on the same host rack U3 and the host-level telemetry shows elevated PCIe bus saturation in the 18:10-18:25 window. That supports the noisy neighbor theory.

bob_sre: We're pausing any cluster-wide driver rollouts until this is cleared. Please don't ship nvidia-driver changes to eu-west1 for now.

alice_oncall: Quick mitigation completed: migrated critical customer pods to healthy hosts, increased replica counts for vulnerable routes temporarily to absorb errors. Implemented temporary autoscaling bump.

dana_ml: Running synthetic load against gpt-medium on healthy hosts to validate behavior. If noisy neighbor induced, healthy hosts shouldn't show AERs under similar load because they're not on the same root complex.

carl_infra: Provider ETA for full hardware check ~24-48h. They recommended we either evict the affected host or wait for their maintenance window. We're requesting immediate quarantine to prevent recurrence.

bob_sre: Next steps for RCA: collect complete kernel + nvidia + hypervisor logs, correlate PCIe AER timestamps with provider-reported noisy neighbor flows, check recent driver/firmware rollouts, and run repro stress test on hardware (with provider supervision).

emily_support: Drafted customer update and shared in #private-customer-commms. Waiting on final timeline to publish.

alice_oncall: Handoff: Bob is primary for the RCA and postmortem. I'm stepping out at 19:10 UTC; leave follow-ups to Bob/carl. @bob_sre please ack takeover.

bob_sre: Ack — taking lead. Will post RCA skeleton in #postmortems after initial artifact upload. Closing live ops loop: node drained, critical traffic migrated, provider engaged. Logging handoff in PD: incident assigned to bob_sre. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty: PagerDuty note: Incident acknowledged by bob_sre, escalation closed.

(between messages: small back-and-forth confirmations, :eyes: reactions, and short logs uploaded).

bob_sre: Final quick note in-thread before formal RCA writeup: most signals point to host-level PCIe fabric saturation from another tenant + GPU resets. Root cause candidate: noisy neighbor saturating PCIe root complex causing AER flood -> GPU resets -> hypervisor watchdog reboots. We'll validate with provider logs and firmware checks.

bob_sre: Action: I'll create the postmortem doc and link artifacts (logs, timeline, hypotheses, vendor SR) by EOD. If anyone finds divergent evidence (driver FW failure pattern or repeated ECC fatal codes), please drop it here.

emily_support: I'll send the post-incident customer update after the EOD RCA draft.

alice_oncall: Thank you all. Leaving thread. :+1:
